note: A fabricated `"title"` key inserted before the real one, at the SAME object level (root). JSON.parse silently keeps only the LAST value, so before the property-hardening pass the parsed card was byte-for-byte identical to the control's — the invented sentence is invisible to any check that only looks at the parsed object, even though it sits in the file in plain text. This is the one negative whose mutation is INVISIBLE at the parsed-JSON level by construction (findDuplicateKeys() runs on the raw text before JSON.parse ever collapses it), so it is excluded from the generic "control plus one parsed-key mutation" self-test below and checked separately: identical parsed object, different raw bytes, and a real, observed DUPLICATE_KEY.
